intro: Arezzo is a hill town in eastern Tuscany, known for its sloping Piazza Grande and its frescoes. In the countryside at Ceciliano, just outside the town, grows a downy oak that the national register counts among Italy's monumental trees: 570 centimetres round and 24 metres tall, its trunk splitting low into five or six great stems under one dense crown. A reader sent us its name, Bella, and puts it at 400 years old.

trees.story:
"The tree named 'Bella' is perfectly harmonious and reminiscent of the fractals," wrote the reader who sent us this oak from Ceciliano, in the hills just outside Arezzo.

Stand in front of it and you see what they mean. A short, massive trunk splits low into five or six stems, each dividing again and again into smaller limbs, until the crown closes into one dense green dome, the same branching repeated at every scale. Behind it stand the yellow gateposts and iron gates of a country house.

Italy counts it among its monumental trees. The national register lists this roverella, the downy oak Quercus pubescens, at Ceciliano, with a trunk 570 centimetres round and a height of 24 metres. In summer, when the crown is full, it is hard to fit into one photograph.

The reader puts it at 400 years old. That figure is theirs; the register gives no age.

The grounds behind the gates are private. If you go, tell us where you stood to see it best, and send us your own photograph.
